concepts.definition: A carboxylic acid with a hydrocarbon chain, the building block of most lipids.
A fatty acid that humans cannot make and must eat: linoleic and alpha-linolenic acid.
The two geometries of a double bond; cis bends the chain, trans keeps it nearly straight.

questions.q: How do saturated, monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids differ?
questions.a: By the number of carbon-carbon double bonds: none, one, or two or more.
